extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors preparing and submitting manuscripts to BMC Microbiology
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing, formatting, and submitting research and other article types to BMC Microbiology, including editorial policies, data and file requirements, peer review expectations, and open access/licencing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aims and scope / suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure you submit to the most suitable journal. BMC Microbiology considers articles on all aspects of microbiology (bacteria, archaea, algae and fungi, viruses, unicellular parasites and helminths) across many sub-topics (applied microbiology, clinical microbiology and vaccines, ecological and evolutionary microbiology, microbe-host interactions, microbial biochemistry/physiology/metabolism, microbial biotechnology, genetics/genomics/proteomics, microbiome, signaling and cellular microbiology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure their manuscript fits the journal’s described topical coverage. As a BMC Series journal, editorial decisions are not based on perceived interest or potential impact; manuscripts are considered for publication if they are scientifically valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific validity criteria for research articles
rubrics_metrics.description: For research articles, this includes having a clearly defined and sound research question, appropriate methodology and analysis, and adherence to community-agreed standards relevant to the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and peer reviewers will assess whether methodology and data support the conclusions. Ensure methods are rigorous and standards (e.g., community-accepted data archiving) are followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access publishing and APCs
rubrics_metrics.description: An article processing charge (APC) applies for each article accepted for publication; the APC price is determined from the date of acceptance. Current APC is listed (e.g. £2390 / $3090 / €2690) and is subject to VAT/local taxes and Springer Nature’s country-tiered pricing pilot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the APC applicable to your country. Funding, institutional agreements, discounts and waivers may apply. Requests for discretionary waivers/discounts must be made at submission; requests during review or after acceptance cannot be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing and copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: Open access articles are published under Creative Commons licences; BMC Microbiology articles are published under CC BY-NC-ND or CC BY. Under Creative Commons licences, authors retain copyright of their articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CC BY-NC-ND allows sharing for non-commercial purposes with credit to authors but requires permission for commercial re-use or derivative versions. CC BY allows sharing and adaptation for any purpose with author credit. Licence variations may be available to meet funder/institutional requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may submit a manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: A manuscript can only be submitted by an author of the manuscript and may not be submitted by a third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure an author performs the online submission; follow the journal’s policies for authorship and declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main manuscript formatting (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quick points: Use double-line spacing; include line and page numbering; use SI units; ensure all special characters are embedded in the text; do not use page breaks in your manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these basic formatting rules so the manuscript converts correctly to PDF and is readable by editors and reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable file formats and editable files requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptable formats for the main manuscript: Microsoft Word (DOC, DOCX), Rich text format (RTF), TeX/LaTeX. Editable files are required for production; non-editable files (such as PDFs) will require re-submission of an editable file during revision or after acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For TeX/LaTeX users: encouraged to use the Springer Nature LaTeX template; all relevant editable source files must be uploaded. Failure to submit source files will delay production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and content of 'Availability of data and materials' section
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about data availability must be detailed in an ‘Availability of data and materials’ section. Required formats: e.g. "The dataset(s) supporting the conclusions of this article is(are) available in the [repository name] repository, [unique persistent identifier and hyperlink ...]." If data are included as additional files: "The dataset(s) supporting the conclusions of this article is(are) included within the article (and its additional file(s))."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide persistent identifiers (DOI, accession numbers). Follow community expectations: where public repository archiving is widely established, deposition is mandatory. BioMed Central endorses Force11 Data Citation Principles and requires fully referencing publicly available datasets in the reference list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and materials — machine-readable and repository guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly encouraged or required to provide all datasets on which conclusions rely, either by depositing in publicly available repositories or presenting them in the main paper/additional files; provide datasets in a machine-readable format (e.g., spreadsheets rather than PDFs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not link to data on personal/departmental websites. For databases include web/ftp address and usage restrictions. For software include: project name, project home page, archived version DOI, operating system(s), programming language, other requirements, license, and any restrictions to use by non-academics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference policy — what to cite
rubrics_metrics.description: Only articles, clinical trial registration records and abstracts that have been published or are in press, or are available through public e-print/preprint servers, may be cited in the reference list. Unpublished abstracts, unpublished data and personal communications should not be included in the reference list but may be included in the text as "unpublished observations" or "personal communications" with the names of the involved researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain permission to quote personal communications. Any in-press articles necessary for reviewer assessment should be made available if requested. Follow journal/article-type reference style and Index Medicus/MEDLINE abbreviations. Use reference management software to ensure correct formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting web links and URLs in references
rubrics_metrics.description: All web links and URLs, including authors' own websites, should be given a reference number and included in the reference list rather than within the text. Provide full details including title, URL, and date accessed (e.g., The Mouse Tumor Biology Database. https://... Accessed 20 May 2013).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an author/group can be clearly associated with a web link (e.g., weblogs), include the author/group in the reference. Avoid placing links directly in the body text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure preparation — numbering, composite panels, titles/legends and keys
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should be numbered in the order first mentioned in the text. Multi-panel figures should be submitted as a single composite file containing all parts. Figure titles (max 15 words) and legends (max 300 words) should be provided in the main manuscript, not in the graphic file. Figure keys should be incorporated into the graphic, not into the legend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload figures in the order they are first mentioned. Ensure figure text and keys appear legibly at final publication dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure file formats, size, resolution and graphic standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted figure file formats: EPS, PDF, Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, TIFF, JPEG, PNG, BMP, CDX. Individual figure files should not exceed 10 MB. Figures in the final PDF should have image resolution approx. 300 dpi at final size; web widths 600 px (standard) or 1200 px (high resolution). Lines wider than 0.25 pt when constrained to standard widths; all fonts must be embedded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vector figures are preferably submitted as PDF. TIFF files should be saved with LZW compression. JPEG files saved at maximum quality. Minimize conversions between file types to avoid degradation. Design figures so all information is legible at standard sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for reproduced figures/tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are responsible for obtaining permission from the copyright holder to reproduce figures or tables that have previously been published elsewhere. Permission should be indicated in the figure legend, and the original source included in the reference list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For open access publication, ensure you have permission to include previously published images; indicate permissions clearly in legends and references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table formatting and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables should be numbered and cited in sequence in the text. Tables less than one A4/Letter page may be placed within the manuscript; tables larger than one page can be placed at the end of the document and large or wide tables can be uploaded as additional files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tabular data as additional files should be uploaded as Excel (.xls) or CSV (.csv) with standard extensions. Table titles (max 15 words) above the table and legends (max 300 words) beneath. Do not embed tables as figures or spreadsheet files; use the 'Table object' function in word processors. Color and shading may not be used; highlight parts using superscript, numbering, lettering, symbols or bold with explanations in legend. Do not use commas to indicate numerical values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing additional files (supplementary material)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can provide datasets, tables, movies or other information as additional files. All additional files will be published with the accepted article. Do not include patient consent forms, certificates of language editing, or revised versions of the main manuscript with tracked changes in additional files (such files should be sent by email if requested).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum file size for additional files is 20 MB each; files will be virus-scanned. Reference each additional file in sequence within the main text and include: file name (e.g., Additional file 1), file format and extension, title of data, and description of data. Results otherwise "data not shown" should be included as additional files. Do not include individual participant details. Avoid linking to data on personal websites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language quality and editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting your work in well-written English gives the best chance for editors and reviewers to understand and evaluate it fairly. Authors may seek help via tutorials, colleagues who are native English speakers, or professional language editing services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer Nature Author Services and partner tools (e.g., AJE language check) are available but their use is not required and does not guarantee editorial acceptance or peer review selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover letter should include: an explanation of why your manuscript should be published in BMC Microbiology, an explanation of any issues relating to journal policies, a declaration of any potential competing interests, confirmation that all authors have approved the manuscript for submission, and confirmation that the content has not been published or submitted elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitting to a special issue, include its specific name in the cover letter. Suggesting peer reviewers and listing excluded reviewers may be included (see reviewer suggestion guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggesting and excluding peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may suggest potential peer reviewers and provide institutional email addresses or information to verify identity (e.g., ORCID or Scopus ID). Authors may also list anyone they prefer not to review their manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intentionally falsifying reviewer information (false names or emails) will result in rejection and possible further misconduct investigation. Prefer institutional emails where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review criteria and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is used to evaluate manuscripts before publication. Typically two or more experts evaluate manuscripts based on three main criteria: scientific robustness (sound methodology and data supporting conclusions), originality (does the research duplicate published work), and clarity (is the manuscript clear and coherent). BMC Microbiology operates a transparent peer review system where reviewer reports are published alongside the article under a Creative Commons Attribution License 4.0, but reviewers are not named.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and editors are required to declare competing interests and may be excluded if such interests exist. Published reviewer reports can aid training and research into peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript transfer process and author control
rubrics_metrics.description: A manuscript transfer provides a way to resubmit your manuscript and reviewer comments to another journal within the Springer Nature portfolio after rejection. Transfer offers present alternative journals; transfers require the author’s input to agree and complete submission to the new journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits include choice of suitable journals and time savings (no reformatting). Authors may decline a transfer via a link in the decision letter or withdraw a transfer at any point by contacting the Transfer Desk; no transfer will occur without author consent.
